data_classes.summary: Provider credentials, Home Assistant authentication context, approval tokens, and recovery keys.
data_classes.handling: Backend-only or platform-owned; never provider context, frontend state, logs, diagnostics, exports, fixtures, or committed evidence.

data_classes.summary: Entity state, attributes, events, presence, security, location, calendar, camera, voice, and notification target data.
data_classes.handling: Deny by default; minimize to an explicit workflow scope and destination policy; redact at every artifact egress.

data_classes.summary: User input, prompts, model-visible context, model output, tool arguments, and tool results.
data_classes.handling: Treat as untrusted; delimit inputs, validate outputs, apply retention policy, and never store hidden reasoning.

data_classes.summary: Provider non-secret options, workflows, routing, model selections, UI preferences, and versioned schemas.
data_classes.handling: Administratively authorized, versioned, validated, migratable, and exported without credentials.

data_classes.summary: Tool definitions, action targets and arguments, risk decisions, confirmations, execution state, and Home Assistant context.
data_classes.handling: Typed and allowlisted; reauthorize before side effects; bind confirmations exactly; never replay unknown outcomes.

data_classes.summary: Redacted health, duration, usage, error class, audit metadata, diagnostics, and support/export artifacts.
data_classes.handling: Bounded retention and recursive redaction; no prompt bodies, credentials, or protected household values by default.

data_classes.summary: Encrypted backups, emergency-kit material, migration data, and restore evidence.
data_classes.handling: Encrypted and stored outside the Home Assistant device; recovery material is never committed; restore tests use spare or isolated systems.

nodes.summary: Authorized administrator or permitted household user.
Bundled AI Orchestrator panel inside an authenticated Home Assistant session.
AI Orchestrator custom-integration backend, policy layer, workflow runtime, redactor, and provider contract.
Home Assistant authentication, registries, state, events, actions, Assist, notifications, and authoritative runtime.
Home Assistant config entries and versioned integration storage.
Explicitly configured local AI endpoint such as LM Studio.
Explicitly configured cloud provider such as Azure OpenAI or AWS Bedrock.
Home Assistant notification, media, voice, or other approved output target.
Logs, diagnostics, traces, exports, screenshots, fixtures, and evidence leaving live memory.
Encrypted local and off-device backup locations plus isolated restore environment.

flows.summary: An authenticated user opens the panel, configures product state, tests, approves, or invokes an allowed feature.
flows.boundary: User intent enters the authenticated browser session.

flows.summary: Home Assistant serves the bundled panel and authenticated product state without provider credentials.
flows.boundary: Home Assistant backend crosses into browser-visible state.

flows.summary: The panel calls typed authenticated WebSocket commands on the integration backend.
flows.boundary: Browser-controlled input crosses into privileged integration code.

flows.summary: Home Assistant supplies selected registries, state, events, action schemas, user context, and Assist input.
flows.boundary: Authoritative Home Assistant data becomes untrusted workflow context.

flows.summary: The backend reads and writes provider configuration, versioned workflows, policy, and bounded history.
flows.boundary: Runtime memory crosses into persistent Home Assistant-owned storage.

flows.summary: A policy-filtered request is sent through the provider contract to an explicitly configured local endpoint.
flows.boundary: Selected context leaves Home Assistant for a LAN provider process.

flows.summary: An explicitly opted-in, policy-filtered request is sent through the provider contract to a cloud provider.
flows.boundary: Approved context leaves the private network for a named cloud destination.

flows.summary: Local provider output returns to the backend for normalization, schema validation, and policy enforcement.
flows.boundary: Untrusted model output re-enters privileged integration code.

flows.summary: Cloud provider output returns to the backend for normalization, schema validation, and policy enforcement.
flows.boundary: Untrusted remote model output re-enters privileged integration code.

flows.summary: A validated and currently authorized structured action is invoked through Home Assistant with its originating context.
flows.boundary: Model-influenced structured data approaches an authoritative side-effect runtime.

flows.summary: The backend returns redacted UI state, destination indicators, validation results, and bounded execution traces.
flows.boundary: Backend state crosses into browser-visible output.

flows.summary: Home Assistant delivers deterministic primary alerts and approved notifications or announcements to configured output targets.
flows.boundary: Home Assistant-controlled output leaves the core runtime for a device or notification service.

flows.summary: Redacted logs, diagnostics, traces, exports, fixtures, and acceptance records leave runtime memory.
flows.boundary: Operational data becomes a persistent or shareable artifact.

flows.summary: Home Assistant creates encrypted backups to local and off-device locations and restores only under the approved recovery procedure.
flows.boundary: Configuration and protected household state leave the live Home Assistant installation for recovery storage or an isolated restore target.

requirements.summary: Configure multiple local and cloud provider connections through the UI behind one provider contract.
Discover current Home Assistant entities, devices, areas, floors, labels, states, and available actions.
Give every agent or workflow separate observation, action, privacy, and confirmation scopes.
Build versioned workflows from triggers, deterministic conditions, constrained AI steps, branches, Home Assistant actions, and explicit failure behavior.
Support compose, classify, extract, predefined-branch choice, and bounded conversation or tool modes.
Provide chat and Home Assistant Assist conversation-agent support.
Deliver announcements and notifications through actions actually available in the live Home Assistant instance.
Support named local and cloud routes, health checks, policy-safe failover, and visible data destinations.
Provide dry runs, exact context previews, redacted traces, and restart-safe workflow behavior.
Support security and event workflows without making AI the primary life-safety detector or unrestricted action authority.
Initial distribution remains private and personal-use oriented.
Home Assistant remains the source of truth for states and device actions.
Provider credentials and requests never originate directly from the browser.
No unrestricted generic Home Assistant action tool is exposed to a model.
Cloud disclosure never occurs without explicit workflow-level authorization.
Generated or edited YAML is not the primary product experience.
No provider or Home Assistant capability is claimed without documentation or live validation.
No high-risk action policy is inferred for the owner.
A capability is accepted only when it is UI-configurable, side-effect safe to test, destination-transparent, offline-tolerant, and traceable with redaction.

controls.summary: Use Home Assistant authentication and context; restrict provider and published-workflow administration to authorized administrators and recheck authorization at use time.
Accept and use credentials only in the backend; never return, log, export, trace, or redirect them to another origin.
Apply central recursive secret and household-data redaction to every egress artifact, with deterministic canary scanning.
Minimize context, default workflows to local-only, require explicit per-workflow cloud opt-in, and filter prohibited fields before destination selection.
Normalize and validate provider schemes, origins, redirects, DNS and IP results, and credential destination before every provider request.
Keep provider-specific behavior behind one contract with probed capabilities, bounded timeouts, cancellation, normalized errors, and truthful unknown states.
Treat model output as untrusted and require strict structured validation before branch, tool, or action use.
Expose only typed, versioned, narrowly allowlisted tools; never expose a generic unrestricted Home Assistant action executor.
Classify risk, prohibit critical model actions, bind confirmations exactly, and revalidate current context, target, arguments, policy, and state immediately before execution.
Journal side effects, prevent duplicate execution and recursive loops, and never automatically replay an unknown or committed outcome during retry, failover, reload, or restart.
Keep life-safety and security detection and primary alerts deterministic; AI enrichment cannot delay, suppress, downgrade, or recall them.
Apply owner-approved bounded retention and explicit deletion semantics to chat, execution metadata, diagnostics, and exports.
Claim compatibility only for named tested Home Assistant versions and verify setup, unload, reload, restart, panel ownership, and version-sensitive migrations.
Use encrypted automatic backups with off-device storage and protected recovery material; test restoration only on spare or isolated Home Assistant systems at the approved cadence.

tests.summary: Verify administrator and non-administrator read, configure, approve, and invoke behavior with preserved Home Assistant context.
Prove browser code receives no provider credential and sends no provider request directly.
Exercise credential create, validation, error, rotation, removal, backup, diagnostics, UI, trace, log, and export paths without secret disclosure.
Scan supported artifacts for deterministic synthetic secret and household canaries.
Capture sanitized local and cloud requests proving destination preview, local default, explicit opt-in, field minimization, prohibited-field filtering, and policy-safe failover.
Test approved and denied URL, redirect, userinfo, IPv4, IPv6, DNS rebinding, metadata, loopback, LAN, and public endpoint cases.
Run every provider adapter against common capability, timeout, cancellation, streaming, usage, tool, schema, and normalized-error cases.
Reject malformed, extra-property, ambiguous, unavailable-target, stale-reference, and policy-expanding provider output.
Prove prompts and provider output cannot add tools, actions, targets, fields, or permissions outside the typed allowlist.
Verify risk policy, prohibited actions, exact confirmation binding, expiry, state recheck, target validation, and authorization immediately before action.
Exercise timeout, retry, failover, reload, restart, cancellation, recursive triggers, and unknown outcomes to prove zero-or-one side effects.
Prove primary life-safety and security alerts still occur under offline, slow, uncertain, malformed, injected, and failed AI paths.
Verify 30-day chat and 90-day execution-metadata defaults, deletion semantics, bounded exports, and no hidden reasoning retention.
Verify named-version setup, unload, reload, restart, panel ownership, non-admin behavior, schema migration, and actual Core upgrade survival.
Verify local-provider authentication rejects missing and invalid credentials, accepts the secret-backed Home Assistant request, and remains reachable after source-scoped firewall hardening.
Verify encrypted automatic backup creation, off-device location, emergency-kit custody, and scheduled retention policy.
Restore an approved backup on a spare or isolated Home Assistant system every six months and after major backup or migration changes; never use production merely to satisfy the test.
Validate catalog schema, global ID uniqueness, reference resolution, requirement coverage, and evidence requirements for verified statuses.
